title: Noetherian underlying finite etale extension
statement: Let $S$ be a qcqs integral scheme whose local rings are integrally closed, and let $c:C\to S$ be a qcqs smooth morphism with geometrically connected fibres and section $\sigma:S\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $K$ for the function field and $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ for the generic-point map. Let $q:C_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $j:C_\eta\to C$ give a pullback square with $i,c$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $s_\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to C_\eta$ satisfy $s_\eta q=1$ and $s_\eta j=i\sigma$. Let $G$ be a finite group whose order is invertible on $S$, and $Z\to C_\eta$ a finite etale $G$-torsor with a $K$-rational point over $s_\eta$ [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Assume additionally that $S$ is Noetherian. Then there are a scheme $P$, a finite etale morphism $\pi:P\to C$, and a map $\psi:Z\to P$ giving a pullback square over $j$. Surjectivity and an action on $P$ are not asserted here.

proof.text:
Over a discrete valuation ring, the special fibre is a regular Cartier divisor.
Ramification indices divide the group order, so the cover is tame. The normalization is
finite locally free and has the standard tame local form (0EYG, 0EYH). The rational point
and the simply transitive action split the fibre over the generic section point. The trait
criterion (0EYI) gives étaleness near the special section point, hence at the generic point
of the irreducible special fibre. Purity (0EYE) extends the cover across that divisor.

Over a Noetherian normal base, choose the maximal open carrying an extension. At a
minimal point of its complement, dimension one is the trait case. In dimension at least
two, normality gives depth at least two, and flatness transfers this to the total space.
The depth-two extension (0EY6) is finite and commutes with flat base change. Complete an
affine neighbourhood along the section: the completion is a power series ring over the
local base. The cover on the punctured section is split, by normality and its split generic
fibre. The full faithfulness theorem (0EY9) makes the cover over the punctured completion
split too. Its depth-two extension is split, so flat descent gives étaleness at the generic
point of the missing fibre; 0EYB gives étaleness everywhere. Spread to a larger open,
contradicting maximality. The action needed during this construction extends by normality.

For a disconnected torsor, the finite group acts transitively on its connected components. Each component is a torsor for its stabilizer and meets the split section fibre. Apply the preceding construction with this subgroup, whose order divides the invertible group order, and induce and take the disjoint union to recover the original torsor. Retain only the underlying finite etale morphism and its generic comparison.
